1.n: mixed aorist ἷξον of ἵκω (= ἱκνέομαι); + acc. of the place reached
'hollow', 'mountain-pent': the deep valley of the Eurotas between Taygetus and Parnon (Merry on 4.1); κοίλην Λακεδαίμονα κητώεσσαν as Iliad 2.581
the district, whose chief town is Sparta (Buttmann, followed by Merry on 4.1)
meaning uncertain ('of ravines' or 'vast'); Zenodotus read καιετάεσσαν, explained as 'full of calamint' (scholia, in Merry on 4.1)

2.n: unaugmented 3 pl. as from a by-form ἐλάω (= ἤλαυνον), as Iliad 24.696; intransitive, 'drove (the chariot)'; not ἑλών 'taking' (αἱρέω)

3.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. masc.
3.n: active 'give a feast', with the occasion in the accusative, as δαινύναι τάφον (3.309) (Merry on 4.3)
'wedding', here the feast; 3–19 were cut by Diodorus the Aristophanean (Athenaeus 5.180), wrongly, Merry thinks (Merry on 4.3)

epic dat. pl. -ῃσι(ν); dative of the guests; ἔται as in Iliad 9.464, 16.456; the scholia explain 'citizens', Apollonius 'companions'; Merry takes them as men of one's own generation, neither kinsmen nor comrades (Merry on 4.3)

4.n: epic gen. υἱέος (stem υἱε-); with γάμον (3): the wedding of his son
with θυγατρός; Bekker (2nd ed.) read ἀμύμονα, holding that the possessive ὅς always began with a digamma (Merry on 4.4)
possessive ὅς (= ἑῷ), not the relative

5.n: 'breaking (the ranks of) men' (ῥήγνυμι + ἀνήρ); in the Iliad only of Achilles (7.228, 13.324, 16.146, 16.575)
epic dat. υἱέϊ (stem υἱε-); Neoptolemus, not named here
unaugmented (= ἔπεμπε); the imperfect, like ἐξετέλειον (7) and ἤγετο (10), of what was in progress (Merry on 4.7)

7.n: epic dat. pl. τοῖσι(ν) = τοῖς: Hermione and the son of Achilles; dative of interest
from the epic by-form ἐκτελείω (= ἐξετέλουν): 'were bringing to accomplishment' (Merry on 4.7); θεοὶ … ἐξετέλειον as Iliad 9.493

8.n: = ἔνθα; 'thither', defined by the next line
uncontracted (Attic νεῖσθαι); infinitive of purpose after πέμπε, as 29 (Merry on 4.8)

9.n: epic dat. pl. οἷσι(ν) = οἷς; dative with ἀνάσσω 'rule over'; antecedent Μυρμιδόνων
unaugmented (= ἤνασσε); the son of Achilles, as king of Phthia (Merry on 4.9)

10.n: epic dat. υἱέϊ (stem υἱε-); Menelaus' son Megapenthes (11)
Σπάρτη + suffix -θεν 'from' (as 2.327); to be joined with Ἀλέκτορος, not ἤγετο, for the wedding was at Sparta (Merry on 4.10)
a Spartan, father of the bride; named only here in Homer
middle 'bring home (a wife)', usually of the bridegroom, here of the father taking a wife for his son, as ἠγάγετο 15.238, ἄξομαι 21.214 (Merry on 4.10)

11.n: antecedent υἱέι (10); Μεγαπένθης stands in the relative clause
sense disputed: 'darling' (as Iliad 9.143) or 'late-born'; Merry (on 4.11) argues for 'grown up', a youth: Megapenthes, born after Helen left, would now be about twenty
'Great Grief' (μέγας + πένθος), a name recalling the sorrow Helen's flight caused (Merry on 4.11); again 15.100, 103, 122

12.n: a captive, not a slave by birth (Merry on 4.12); some ancients took Δούλη as her name (scholia, in Merry on 4.12); in Homer again only Iliad 3.409
dative of interest; Rhianus and Aristophanes read Ἑλένης (scholia, in Merry on 4.12)
'brought to light': granted no more children

13.n: ἐπεὶ δή 'once, after', a line opening again 8.452, 21.25 (Merry on 4.13)
adverbial with τό: 'first, once for all'

14.n: Helen's daughter, named only here in Homer (unnamed at Iliad 3.175); in apposition to παῖδʼ (13); Ἑρμιόνη at Iliad 2.560 is a town of the Argolid
Ionic gen. -ης; -εη- scanned as one syllable (synizesis)

15.n: unaugmented (= ἐδαίνυντο); middle 'feast'; 15–19 were said in antiquity to be Aristarchus' work, not Homer's, brought over from Iliad 18.604–606 (scholia; Athenaeus 5.180); Merry thinks Aristarchus rather marked them as doubtful (Merry on 4.15–19)
= κατά; τ → θ before rough breathing

16.n: in apposition to οἱ (15); in Homer only in the Odyssey (again 5.489, 9.48)
not elided before ἔται, originally ϝέται

17.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.
17.n: middle 'take delight'; 17–18 = Iliad 18.604–605, where Athenaeus says Aristarchus removed the words μετὰ … φορμίζων

18.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

18.n: dual; 'tumblers', from κυβιστάω 'leap head first' (Cretan κύβη 'head') (Merry on 4.18)

19.p: verb · pres. part. act. gen. sg. masc.
19.n: genitive absolute, sc. ἀοιδοῦ: the singer leads off, as ἐξῆρχε γόοιο Iliad 18.51 (Merry on 4.19); Iliad 18.606 has ἐξάρχοντες, of the tumblers, and Aristarchus read that here too (Athenaeus, in Merry on 4.19)
intransitive 'spin'; plural with the dual subject
epic μέσσος = μέσος: 'through the middle (of them)', defining κατʼ αὐτούς (18) more nearly (Merry on 4.19)

20.n: dual: Telemachus and Peisistratus; subject of στῆσαν (22)
epic dat. pl. -οισι; the entrance from outside into the courtyard (Merry on 4.20)
dual: the men, as against the horses

21.n: in apposition to τώ (20); accent from enclitic θʼ
= τε (θ before rough breathing); τε … καί 'both … and'

22.n: unaugmented root aorist (= ἔστησαν, of ἔστην), intransitive: 'halted'
Eteoneus, named at the end of the line

22.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

22.n: unaugmented middle aorist (= εἴδετο), same sense as active
participial form 'ruling'; the title implies that Eteoneus was of gentle birth (Merry on 4.22); the scholia make him a kinsman of Menelaus (in Merry on 4.22)
Menelaus' attendant, again 15.95; not Eteonus, the Boeotian town (Iliad 2.497)

23.n: 'ready, nimble'; ὀτρηρὸς θεράπων, as the dual at Iliad 1.321
a free companion in service, not a slave

24.n: unaugmented root aorist (= ἔβη); βῆ δʼ ἴμεν 'set out to go'

24.p: verb · fut. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
24.n: uncontracted future participle (Attic ἀγγελῶν), of purpose
ποιμὴν λαῶν 'shepherd of the people': Menelaus; dative with ἀγγελέων

25.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

26.n: dual of τις: 'two strangers, whoever they are'
dual: 'here, yonder', with a gesture (Merry on 4.26)

27.n: Ionic γενεή; dative with ἔικτον: like the race of Zeus, i.e. royal, as kings are διογενεῖς and διοτρεφεῖς (Merry on 4.27)
dual of the perfect ἔοικα (stem ϝε-ϝικ-) with present sense, + dat.; Nitzsch, with a few manuscripts, prefers the commoner pluperfect ἐίκτην (Merry on 4.27)

28.n: first member of a double question, answered by ἦ (29)
dual (enclitic σφωϊν): the two strangers; dative of interest
short-vowel aorist subjunctive (= καταλύσωμεν), deliberative, beside πέμπωμεν (29), or future indicative; 'loose (the horses) from the chariot'

29.n: circumflexed ἦ in the second member of a double question
object of ἱκανέμεν: join ἢ πέμπωμεν ἱκανέμεν ἄλλον ὅς κε (Merry on 4.29)
epic infinitive -έμεν (= ἱκάνειν), of purpose after πέμπωμεν, as 8 (Merry on 4.8)
'entertain as a guest'; subjunctive with κε of the expected case; Aristarchus seems to have read the future φιλήσει (Dindorf, in Merry on 4.29)

30.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
30.n: 'be vexed, troubled'; the line = Iliad 17.18, and again 332

31.n: patronymic of Eteoneus (as 15.95, 140); Βοηθόος 'running to help', as the adjective at Iliad 13.477

32.n: emphatic: ἀτὰρ μὲν νῦν γε 'but now at any rate', as Iliad 6.125
postpositive ὡς 'like', accented after its noun

33.n: epic = ξένια: the food and drink set before a guest
the stress lies on ξεινήια πολλὰ φαγόντε: many hospitalities enjoyed, so let us not refuse it to others (Merry on 4.34)

33.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. du. masc.
33.n: dual participle of the aorist φαγεῖν, which serves ἐσθίω; 'having eaten', with ἱκόμεθʼ (34); Bekker, with the Harleian manuscript, reads the plural φαγόντες (Merry on 4.33)

34.n: genitive of source with ξεινήια (33): the hospitality of other men
epic αἰ = εἰ; αἴ κε 'in the hope that': 'we are come here in the hope that Zeus may rid us of sorrow' (Merry on 4.34)
epic = ἄν; accent from enclitic ποθι

35.n: of time: 'in the time to come'
stresses ἐξοπίσω: hereafter at least, for the past had been hard enough (Merry on 4.34)
subjunctive with αἴ κε (34); + gen.: 'stop (someone) from'
'woe, misery'; genitive of separation with παύσῃ

36.n: in tmesis: ἐς … ἄγε = εἴσαγε; 'bring them forward into the house' (Merry on 4.36)
aorist passive with middle sense 'feast'; infinitive of purpose; only here in Homer

37.n: = φάτο (τ → θ before rough breathing); unaugmented (= ἔφατο)
epic gen. -οιο; genitive of the space crossed; the vulgate has ὁ δʼ ἐκ μεγάροιο, but Aristarchus read it without ἐκ (scholia, in Merry on 4.37)
root aorist (cf. ἐσσύμην from σεύω) with δια-; + gen.
reduplicated aorist of κέλομαι; + acc. and inf.: 'called on (them) to'

38.n: 2nd aorist ἑσπόμην (stem σπ-); Bekker, from the Harleian manuscript, reads ἅμα σπέσθαι for ἅμʼ ἑσπέσθαι, σπέσθαι being the more genuine form (Merry on 4.38)
epic ἑοῖ = οἷ; with αὐτῷ, reflexive: 'with himself'

39.n: unaugmented (= ἔλυσαν); join ὑπὸ ζυγοῦ λῦσαν, as ὑπʼ ἀπήνης … ἔλυον 7.5–6 (Merry on 4.39)

39.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. pl. masc.

40.n: the horses; the line as Iliad 8.434, with ἱππείῃσι for ἀμβροσίῃσι
epic dat. pl. -ῃσι; 'of horses', as φάτνῃ ἐφʼ ἱππείῃ Iliad 10.568

41.n: epic apocopated πάρ = παρά; in tmesis with ἔβαλον (παραβάλλω 'throw beside')
in tmesis: πὰρ … ἔβαλον = παρέβαλον; of fodder thrown to horses, as Iliad 5.369
'spelt', a kind of wheat, as ὀλύραι (Iliad 5.196) is rendered; which grain is meant is much disputed; Herodotus (2.36) says some call ὀλύραι ζειαί (Merry on 4.41); in Homer only here and 604
in tmesis with ἔμιξαν (ἀναμίσγω 'mix in with')
in tmesis: ἀνὰ … ἔμιξαν = ἀνέμιξαν; aorist of μίσγω

42.n: plural for a single chariot; the line = Iliad 8.435
'front walls' (ἐν + ὤψ 'face'): the inner faces of the gateway into the court (Nitzsch, in Merry on 4.42)

42.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. pl. neut.
42.n: epic diectasis (= παμφανῶντα); 'lit by the sun or the moon' (scholia), shining in the open gateway (Merry on 4.42)

43.n: the men, as against the horses and chariot
acc. of goal; δόμος, properly the hall, is narrower than δῶμα (44), the whole building (Merry on 4.43)
not elided before ἰδόντες, originally ϝιδόντες

43.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
43.n: aor. εἶδον serves as aorist of ὁράω

45.n: ὥς τε 'just as'; accent from enclitic τε; short for αἴγλη πέλεν ὥς τε ἠελίου αἴγλη (Merry on 4.45); the line again 7.84

46.n: = κατά; τ → θ before rough breathing; placed between noun and adjective

47.n: unaugmented 2nd aorist passive (= ἐτάρπησαν): 'had their fill of', with the participle

47.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.
47.n: middle with active sense; the present of leisurely gazing, against the single glance of ἰδόντες (43) (Merry on 4.47)

48.n: Ionic ἐς = εἰς; accent from enclitic ῥα; the line = Iliad 10.576

48.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

49.n: the guests; the line as Iliad 24.587 (τόν), again 17.88

50.n: the cloak, the outer garment that catches the eye, is named before the tunic (Merry on 4.50)
'woolly, thick', of the root of Latin vellus, English 'wool' (Curtius, in Merry on 4.50); a different word from οὖλος 'baneful'

51.n: Ionic ἐς = εἰς; accent from enclitic ῥα

52.n: 'pitcher, ewer' (προχέω 'pour forth'); join προχόῳ φέρουσα (Merry on 1.136)
epic aorist ἔχευα (Attic ἐπέχεε): poured the water over (the hands)

52.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. fem.

53.n: held under the hands while the water is poured over them (Merry on 1.138)

54.n: 'smoothed' (ξέω 'scrape'); a scholion records a variant χρυσῆν 'golden' (Merry on 4.54)
epic -σσ-; 'stretched out', i.e. set (the table) in place

55.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. fem.

56.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. fem.
verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. fem.
verb · pres. part. act. gen. pl. neut.

57.n: 'carver', who divides the meat into portions; 57–58 are missing in the Harleian and several other manuscripts, and most editors after Wolf rejected them (Merry on 4.57)

57.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

58.n: epic σφι = αὐτοῖς: Telemachus and Peisistratus

59.n: dual; object of δεικνύμενος and προσέφη; the line as Iliad 9.196

59.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

60.n: = τε (θ before rough breathing); τε καί 'both … and'

61.n: genitive with πασσαμένω; the travellers' first regular meal, though the day was far spent; at 213 it is called δόρπον (Merry on 4.61)

61.p: verb · aor. part. mid. acc. du. masc.
61.n: dual, with the understood object of εἰρησόμεθʼ ('you two'); epic -σσ- (aorist ἐπασάμην), + gen.; a few manuscripts read παυσαμένω (Merry on 4.61)
οἵ τινες written apart = οἵτινες, in an indirect question; plural relative with the dual verb ἐστον, as Iliad 9.198
with οἵ; accent from enclitic ἐστον

62.n: contracted from σφῶιν, only here (Merry on 4.62): 'the lineage of your parents is not lost in you', i.e. in your persons; 62–64 were athetized by Zenodotus and Aristophanes, in part for this un-Homeric monosyllable (scholia, in Merry on 4.62)
intransitive 2nd perfect: 'is lost'; with the dative, as ἀπό τέ σφισιν ὕπνος ὄλωλεν Iliad 10.186 (Merry on 4.62)

63.n: genitive of descent after ἐστέ, as Iliad 21.186–187; in apposition to διοτρεφέων βασιλήων, genus to species (Merry on 4.63)

64.n: 'bearing the scepter' (σκῆπτρον + ἔχω), the mark of a king
ἐπεὶ οὔ κε = οὐ γάρ κε, as Iliad 15.228 (Merry on 4.64)
substantive: 'men of no worth', the low-born

65.n: plural for singular: the chine, the portion of honor, as 8.475, 14.437, Iliad 7.321 (Merry on 4.65)
unaugmented (= ἔθηκεν); in tmesis: παρὰ … θῆκεν

66.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

66.n: article used as relative (= ἅ); antecedent νῶτα (65)
epic enclitic ῥα = ἄρα; accent from enclitic οἱ
contracted from γέραα; predicate; a plural of amplification, not assimilated to νῶτα (Merry on 4.66)
οἱ … αὐτῷ 'himself': Menelaus, having eaten already, gives his guests his own portion (Merry on 4.65)

67.n: the guests; the line = 1.149, Iliad 9.91, 9.221, 24.627, and again 218
= ἐπί; with acc. of goal: 'to (the food)'
= ὀνείατα (τ → θ before rough breathing); ὄνειαρ 'benefit': the good things of the feast

67.p: verb · pres. part. mid. acc. pl. neut.

67.n: ἰάλλω 'send, stretch out': 'they reached out their hands'

68.n: tmesis (ἐξ … ἕντο): 'put from themselves'; unaugmented root aorist of ἵημι (= εἷντο)

70.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
70.n: aorist ἔσχον, the first moment of ἔχων: 'putting (his head) near' (Merry on 1.157)
= πευθοίατο, epic 3 pl. -οίατο (= πεύθοιντο); from the epic by-form πεύθομαι (= πυνθάνομαι); πευθοίαθʼ οἱ ἄλλοι is Zenodotus' reading, Aristarchus read πευθοίατο ἄλλοι (scholia, in Merry on 4.70)

71.n: with demonstrative force: τῷ ἐμῷ θυμῷ 'this heart of mine' (Merry on 4.71)

71.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. voc. sg. masc.
71.n: 'pleasing, dear to' + dat.: 'dear to my heart'

72.n: 'lightning', here the flash of metal (as Iliad 11.83); object of φράζεο (71)
epic apocopated κάδ = κατά, assimilated before δ; so Bekker; the manuscripts give καὶ δώματα (Merry on 4.72)

73.n: 'amber', as in the necklaces of 15.460 and 18.296, the only other places in Homer; Pliny took it here for electrum, the pale alloy of gold and silver, as its place between them suggests, but the necklaces require amber (Merry on 4.73, after Buttmann)

74.n: epic gen. Ζηνός (= Διός); accent from enclitic που
the court as seen on entering, or loosely the dwelling itself, as Iliad 24.452 (Merry on 4.74); Seleucus read τοιαῦτα δόμοις ἐν κτήματα κεῖται, avoiding αὐλή (Athenaeus 188f, in Merry on 4.74)

75.n: epic ὅσσος = ὅσος; exclamatory: 'for the untold multitude of the things here', roughly ὅτι τόσα (Merry on 4.75)
'awe, amazement'; σέβας μʼ ἔχει εἰσορόωντα as 3.123, again 142

75.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. masc.

76.p: verb · pres. part. act. gen. sg. masc.

76.n: ξυν- = συν-; unaugmented thematic 2nd aorist middle, + gen.: 'caught (his words)'; this form only here in Homer

77.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

78.n: epic Ζηνί = Διί; dative with ἐρίζοι
'rival', 'vie with' (+ dat.); potential optative with ἄν

79.n: predicate, agreeing with the nearer δόμοι

80.n: partitive with τις; opposed to Ζηνί (78) (Merry on 4.80)
ἤ … ἠὲ καὶ οὐκί 'either … or not', in effect 'few or none', like the later ἤ τις ἢ οὐδείς (Merry on 4.80)
epic = ἄν, with the subjunctive; accent from enclitic τις
short-vowel aorist subjunctive (= ἐρίσσηται), with κεν (Merry on 4.80), or future; epic -σσ-
epic οὐκί = οὐκ, at verse end: 'or not'

81.n: gives the reason why few, if any, can vie with him (Merry on 4.80)

81.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
verb · aor. part. pass. nom. sg. masc.
81.n: aorist passive of ἐπαλάομαι 'wander over', with active sense; πολλὰ παθὼν καὶ πόλλʼ ἐπαληθείς again 15.176

82.n: reduplicated aorist ἠγαγόμην; middle 'brought home for myself', sc. κτήματα (Merry on 4.82)
epic ὀγδόατος = ὄγδοος; the year in which Orestes took vengeance (3.306)

83.n: the land of the Φοίνικες (Iliad 23.744); again 14.291
the adjective (Iliad 9.382) as the people's name; scanned as three syllables, as at 127 (Merry on 4.83)

83.p: verb · aor. part. pass. nom. sg. masc.
83.n: 'having roamed over', + acc.; the scholia gloss πλανηθείς; some read ἐπʼ ἀληθεῖς, 'to the truthful (Egyptians)', skilled in prophecy (scholia, in Merry on 4.83)

84.n: accusative of the goal; accent from enclitic θʼ
the people of Sidon, here as at Iliad 23.743–744 distinguished from the Phoenicians (Merry on 4.84)

named only here in Homer; Aristarchus' reading, where Crates wrote Ἐρεμνούς and Zeno Ἄραβας; taken in antiquity for Troglodytes or Arabs (Strabo 16); perhaps 'the dark people' (cf. ἔρεβος) (Merry on 4.84)

85.n: the land west of Egypt; again 14.295
local 'where'; Herodotus (4.29), quoting the line, has ὅθι (Merry on 4.85)
= τε; epic τε in a statement of what is always so
'come to be, prove'; Herodotus took the line 'begin at once to grow horns', Merry rather 'are horned at once', born with horns sprouting, as Aristotle has it (Hist. Anim. 8.28) (Merry on 4.85)

86.n: some wrote δίς 'twice', absurdly (scholia, in Merry on 4.86)
singular verb with the neuter plural μῆλα; Bekker (2nd ed.) moves the line after 89 (Merry on 4.86)
'bringing to fulfillment' (τέλος + φέρω), the fixed epithet of the year, 'the maturing year'; in Homer only in this phrase (Merry on 4.86), as Iliad 19.32

87.n: οὔτε … οὔτε 'neither … nor'; not elided before ἄναξ, originally ϝάναξ
'lord, master': the owner of the flocks

89.n: the subject is μῆλα (86), now with a plural verb
taken of old as 'lasting the year round' (ἐπί + ἔτος), by Curtius as 'ever-present' (ἐπί + αἰεί): 'plentiful, unfailing' (Merry on 4.89)
'to suck', athematic infinitive of θάομαι (cf. θήσατο μαζόν Iliad 24.58); infinitive of purpose (Merry on 4.89)

90.n: epic ἧος = ἕως, answered by τῆος (91)

90.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

91.n: epic τῆος = τέως, answering ἧος (90); accent from enclitic μοι

92.n: 'unexpectedly', from οἴω 'expect', like Latin necopinato (Merry on 4.92); only here in Homer (adjective ἀνώϊστος Iliad 21.39)
'accursed, ruinous', an aorist participle of ὄλλυμι used as an adjective

93.n: the particle 'surely', not σοι; οὔ τοι with Dindorf and Bekker, from the Harleian manuscript, for οὔ τι (Merry on 4.93)

93.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

93.n: epic dat. pl. -εσσι(ν); dative with ἀνάσσω; after this line some inserted οὐδέ τι βουλόμενος, ἀλλὰ κρατερῆς ὑπʼ ἀνάγκης, which a scholion rightly calls absurd (Merry on 4.93)

94.n: καὶ πατέρων … εἰσίν (94–95) is a parenthesis (Merry on 4.94)
looks forward to the former state of his house (95–96) (Merry on 4.94)
= μέλλετε; of likelihood: 'you are likely to have heard' (Merry on 4.94)
dative of possession: '(who) are your (fathers)'; one scholion reads ὕμμιν (Merry on 4.94)

95.n: explains οὔ τοι χαίρων … ἀνάσσω (93), past the parenthesis (Merry on 4.94)
transitive: 'lost'; his own house, left to waste while he was at Troy, not Priam's, as a scholion wondered (Merry on 4.95)

96.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. masc.

epic -φι ending, here as genitive with ἐξ

'milk-sucking' (γάλα 'milk' + θῆσθαι 'suck'); in Homer only here and 17.127

'son of Philomela' (or of Philomelus); a king of Lesbos, says Eustathius, who challenged all comers to wrestle, the Achaeans too when they put in there (Merry on 4.343); in Homer only here and 17.134

Proteus (385); γέρων ἅλιος 'the Old Man of the Sea', in the Iliad Nereus (1.538, 18.141); again 384, 401, 542

best taken with ἔσχον (352), δεῦρο with νέεσθαι; or ἔτι μεμαῶτα 'while I was still striving to come here' (Merry on 4.351)

perfect with present sense 'be mindful of', + gen.; the subject, men, understood
Ionic gen. pl. -έων (Attic -ῶν); a scholion takes it of sacrifices (θυσιῶν) (Merry's critical note on 4.353)

accented ἔστι 'there is', opening the description of a place
'loud-dashing' (πολύς + κλύζω 'dash, wash'); in Homer only in this phrase (6.204, 19.277)

reduplicated form of καλέω; + two accusatives; the subject, 'men', indefinite

relative, referring to νηῦς (356): dative with ἐπιπνείῃσιν
epic πνείω = πνέω; epic subj. -ῃσι(ν), in a general clause

358.n: 'with good moorings' (ἐϋ- + ὅρμος); ἐν δὲ λιμὴν ἐύορμος again 9.136
= τε; of what is always done
in tmesis with βάλλουσιν (ἀποβάλλω): 'push off' (Merry on 4.358)

'strong'; derived from ἶφι-τιμή or ἶφι-θυμός, most simply from ἶφι alone (Merry on 4.365)

369.n: 'fish-hook'; epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); in Homer only in this line, again 12.332

uncontracted -εαι (= τέρπῃ); middle 'take delight', with the participle πάσχων

794.n: 'joints, limbs' (ἅπτω 'fasten'); uncontracted; in Homer only here and 18.189

795.n: = ἄλλο; ἔνθʼ αὖτʼ ἄλλʼ ἐνόησε is a phrase of the Odyssey (2.382, 2.393), in the Iliad only 23.140, 193

796.n: the dream figure is no creation of the sleeper's mind but has a being of its own (Merry on 4.796); as the phantom of Aeneas, Iliad 5.449
epic pluperfect middle (= ἐῴκει), + dat.: 'it was like'; cf. ἔϊκτο Iliad 23.107

798.n: son of Admetus and Alcestis (Iliad 2.713–715), who lived at Pherae by Lake Boebeis in Thessaly and fought at Troy (Merry on 4.798)
epic dat. pl. -ῇς; Eumelus' Pherae in Thessaly (Iliad 2.711), not Diocles' Pherae (Φηρή, 3.488)
epic ἐνί = ἐν; after its noun, accent thrown back (anastrophe)
epic οἰκία 'dwellings', plural for one house

798.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

799.n: the phantom, as the woman it resembles

800.n: epic ἧος = ἕως, properly 'while', here final 'that', with the optative, as 6.80; a use not found in the Iliad (Merry on 4.800)

800.p: verb · pres. part. mid. acc. sg. fem.
verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. fem.

801.n: optative of purpose after the past πέμπε (799); Aeolic-type aorist optative -ειε; + acc. and gen. 'make (someone) cease from'
epic gen. -οιο; second accent from enclitic τε

802.n: 'along, past': through the slit in which the strap of the bolt worked (cf. Merry on 4.838)
the bar inside the door, drawn by a strap from outside (cf. 1.442)

803.n: unaugmented root aorist (= ἔστη); the line = Iliad 23.68, 24.682, as dream figures stand over the sleeper
in tmesis with ἔειπεν (προσεῖπον 'speak to'), with two accusatives, μιν and μῦθον (Merry on 4.803)
epic ἔειπε (= εἶπε); in tmesis with πρός

804.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. nom. sg. fem.
804.n: perfect participle 'grieved'; φίλον τετιημένη ἦτορ as Iliad 8.437

805.n: οὐ … οὐδέ, the second negative repeating the first (Merry on 4.805, referring to 3.27)

805.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
805.n: epic ζώω = ζάω; θεοὶ ῥεῖα ζώοντες as Iliad 6.138

806.n: perfect ἀκάχημαι 'be grieved', present in sense
'destined to return' (νόστος); predicate; second accent from enclitic ἐστι

807.n: ethical dative, 'in the eyes of the gods', since ἀλιταίνω takes an accusative (Merry on 4.807)

807.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.
807.n: athematic aorist participle, accented as Aristarchus wrote it, not a perfect; almost 'a sinner' (Merry on 4.807); only here in Homer; second accent from enclitic ἐστι

809.n: = κνώσσουσα; 'sleep, slumber'; only here in Homer
'of dreams' (ὄνειρος); epic dat. pl. -ῃσι; only here in Homer; for the gates of dreams cf. 19.562 (Merry on 4.809)

811.n: = πωλέαι (La Roche) or πωλέ(αι): 'come and go, frequent'; with πάρος the tense is present, as regularly (Merry on 4.811)
plural for one house; δώματα ναίειν 'dwell'

813.n: Ionic gen. pl. (= πολλῶν), with ὀδυνάων (812)
κατὰ φρένα καὶ κατὰ θυμόν, as Iliad 1.193

815.n: epic dat. pl. -ῃσι; dative of respect

815.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. acc. sg. masc.
815.n: perfect of καίνυμαι, properly 'be adorned', hence 'excel' (Merry on 4.725)

816.n: ἐσθλόν repeated from 814; the scholia call the line superfluous, as at 726 (Merry's critical note on 4.816)
= κατά; τ → θ before rough breathing
with μέσον Ἄργος apparently a phrase for all Greece, as 1.344

818.n: as the young Achilles, νήπιον, οὔ πω εἰδόθʼ ὁμοιΐου πολέμοιο οὐδʼ ἀγορέων (Iliad 9.440–441) (Merry on 4.818)

818.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

820.n: 'tremble for' (ἀμφί + τρέμω), + gen.; only here in Homer
epic subj. -ῃσι(ν); after μή of fearing; μή τι πάθῃσιν, a euphemism for death, as 12.321 (Merry on 4.820)

821.n: ὅ γε takes up the subject again
antecedent of ἵνα: 'in the land of those where he is gone' (Merry on 4.821)
= ἵνα 'where': the place where he now is, not whither he has gone (Merry on 4.821)

823.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.
823.n: middle ἵεμαι 'press on, be eager', + inf.
infinitive with πρίν; the line again 13.426, 15.30

824.n: neuter, agreeing with εἴδωλον; the line again 835
'dim, faint': from ἀ- privative and the root of μαρμαίρω 'sparkle' (Curtius), or with a euphonic ἀ-, of the wavering glimmer of a dream (Merry on 4.824); in Homer only here and 835

825.n: strengthens the negative, 'by no means', rather than going with λίην (Merry on 4.825)
perfect imperative of δείδια, present in sense

827.n: epic inf. -άμεναι (= παρεστάναι); intransitive: 'stand beside (to help)'

828.n: epic by-form Ἀθηναίη; in apposition to πομπός (826)

828.p: verb · pres. part. mid. acc. sg. fem.

829.n: epic aorist -έηκε (= προῆκε): 'sent forth', + inf.; προέηκε τεῒν τάδε μυθήσασθαι as Iliad 11.201

831.n: εἰ μὲν δή … εἰ δʼ ἄγε (832): 'if indeed …, come then'
epic gen. -οιο; second accent from enclitic τε; 'you have heard the bidding of some god', i.e. come at a god's command (Merry on 4.831)

832.n: epic κεῖνος = ἐκεῖνος: Odysseus; accusative with κατάλεξον, as with ἀγορεύσω (836) (Merry on 4.832)

833.n: contracted (= ὁράει); ζώει καὶ ὁρᾷ φάος ἠελίοιο as Iliad 18.61

834.n: ἦ = ἤ 'or', so accented in the second member of a double question
epic dat. pl. -οισι; plural for one house

835.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. neut.

836.n: epic κεῖνος = ἐκεῖνος; second accent from enclitic γε; accusative with ἀγορεύσω, as with κατάλεξον (832)
adverb of διηνεκής 'continuous': 'from first to last, in full'; in Homer only in the Odyssey (7.241, 12.56)

837.n: epic ζώω = ζάω; ζώει … ἦ τέθνηκε '(whether) he lives or is dead', the question left open, as 2.132; the line again 11.464
ἦ = ἤ 'or', so accented in the second member of a double question

838.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. neut.

838.n: epic gen. -οιο; 'doorpost': 'past the bolt (that fitted) in the doorpost', through the slit in which the strap (802) worked (Merry on 4.838)
unaugmented (= ἐλιάσθη); passive form, middle sense: 'withdrew'

840.n: Ionic κούρη = κόρη; in apposition to ἡ (839)

841.n: ὡς, accented before enclitic οἱ: 'so (clearly)', giving the reason for her cheer
'clear' in its meaning to the mind, though 'dim' (824) to the senses (Merry on 4.841); ἐναργής 'in plain sight' at 3.420
epic athematic aorist (ἐπεσσύμην): the swiftness with which the phantom had come to her (Merry on 4.841)
sense and derivation disputed: 'the dead (darkest part) of night'; some relate ἀμολγός to ἀμαυρός, others take μολγός as 'cloud' (Hesychius) (Merry on 4.841); νυκτὸς ἀμολγῷ as Iliad 11.173

842.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
842.n: 'going on board': the actual departure, after the supper of 786 (Merry on 4.785)
fem. noun with neuter plural κέλευθα

843.n: 'steep': of sudden death, 'headlong, sheer'; φόνον αἰπύν as Iliad 17.365

843.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

844.n: accented ἔστι 'there is', at the head of a description

845.n: epic μεσσηγύ(ς) 'between'; the second half as 671
epic gen. -οιο; second accent from enclitic τε; the island beside Ithaca, as 671

846.n: 'starry' (cf. ἀστήρ); only here in Homer; Merry rejects the identification by modern geographers with the rock of Deskalio (Daskalio) (Merry on 4.846)
ἔνι = ἔνεισι 'are in': the adverb with the verb understood, accent thrown back; + dat. αὐτῇ
'giving anchorage' (ναῦς + λοχ- 'lie'); in Homer again only 10.141

847.g: with an entrance on either side
847.n: 'double', open on both sides (ἀμφί + -δυμος as in δίδυμος 'twin'); only here in Homer
dat. fem. of ὁ used as adverb of place

847.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

847.n: the suitors and their crew, Ithacans, as Achaeans
